milestone.describes: The welcome screen is drawn and stays up: the wooden maze box, the instruction to hold the device parallel to the floor, and a bar along the bottom with Play, Settings and Credits. Play opens the level-pack list, which is further than the rating goes - see the note.

steps.expect: The welcome screen: the maze box photograph, 'Welcome to Labyrinth', and the instruction to tilt.
Still there. This is the two-star milestone.
The level-pack list: a header reading 'Demo levels, By: Rod Ferguson'. The rows below it are dark and it is not established whether they are missing or simply unlit.

notes: Coordinates are client coordinates for the 320x480 portrait window. A capture includes the window border and title bar, so a position read off a frame is about (8, 31) out.

**Play only works from `6dd4671e` onwards.** Before that the bar swallowed every touch: a toolbar decoded from a nib had no items and was an invisible solid rectangle over the app's own artwork. See `dev-docs/app-notes/labyrinth.md`.

The route stops at the pack list because tapping a pack sends the app's own `initGLAndApp` to its own `LevelStatusView`, which tapHLE cannot find. That is the frontier, and it is a class-loading gap rather than a missing framework method.
